description: A six-panel composite of inverse pole figure (IPF) EBSD maps of SLM-printed Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni low-density steel, all rendered in the same rainbow orientation colouring keyed to the triangular "Austenite phase" IPF legend at lower right (vertices labelled 001, 101 and 111, blue-to-red gradient). Every panel carries a black 50 µm scale bar, so all six maps are at the same magnification. (a)–(e) are marked "x-y" in their top-right corners (transverse cross-sections) and, per the caption, correspond to the laser-power samples P-70, P-90, P-110, P-130 and P-150; each shows fine equiaxed grains in random orientations — a mixed red/green/blue/purple mosaic with no dominant hue — with the coloured regions appearing finest and most fragmented in (a) and coarsest in (d) and (e). (f) is marked "x-z" and shows the longitudinal section of P-110, where grains are strongly elongated along the vertical (build) direction, with only a small fraction of finer equiaxed regions. No orientation values, misorientation angles or grain-size numbers are printed anywhere. The group demonstrates that all transverse sections are equiaxed and texture-free, whereas the vertical section develops elongated columnar grains through the melt pools.

subfigures.description: IPF EBSD map marked 'x-y' with a 50 µm scale bar; fine equiaxed grains in many random orientations (mixed red, green, blue, purple), grain coloured regions appearing small and fragmented. Caption assigns it to sample P-70.
IPF EBSD map marked 'x-y' with a 50 µm scale bar; equiaxed multi-coloured grain mosaic similar to (a), with several slightly larger pink/red and green grains. Caption assigns it to sample P-90.
IPF EBSD map marked 'x-y' with a 50 µm scale bar; equiaxed grains, predominantly green/blue with scattered red and yellow grains, no preferred colour. Caption assigns it to sample P-110.
IPF EBSD map marked 'x-y' with a 50 µm scale bar; appearance coarser than (a)–(c), with larger magenta/pink and blue grains separated by fine-grained bands. Caption assigns it to sample P-130.

IPF EBSD map marked 'x-y' with a 50 µm scale bar; coarse equiaxed grains dominated by yellow/orange, violet and blue regions, still with randomly mixed orientations. Caption assigns it to sample P-150.

IPF EBSD map marked 'x-z' with a 50 µm scale bar showing the longitudinal section of P-110; strongly elongated, vertically aligned (columnar) grains in blue/green/red, plus a minor fine equiaxed component.
Triangular IPF colour key labelled 'Austenite phase' with vertices 001 (lower left), 101 (lower right) and 111 (top) and a blue–green–red gradient used for all six maps.

observations.observation: All six panels (a)–(f) are inverse pole figure (IPF) EBSD maps coloured with the same rainbow scheme, each containing a black '50 µm' scale bar.
Panels (a)–(e) are annotated 'x-y' in their top-right corners and panel (f) is annotated 'x-z', indicating transverse versus longitudinal sections.
The colour key at lower right is labelled 'Austenite phase' and is a triangular IPF with vertices 001, 101 and 111, i.e. the maps show the austenite (fcc) phase only.
Panels (a)–(e) display fine equiaxed grains with random orientations, visible as a multi-coloured red/green/blue/purple mosaic with no dominant hue.
Panel (f) shows grains that are strongly elongated and aligned vertically (along the build direction), forming a columnar morphology, plus a small fraction of finer equiaxed regions.
The coloured grain regions appear coarser in (d) and (e) than in (a) and (b), where they are smaller and more fragmented; no grain-size numbers are printed to quantify this.
No orientation values, misorientation angles or grain-size figures are printed on any panel; the only quantitative marker is the 50 µm scale bar.

The caption states that (a)–(e) are IPFs of transverse cross-sections of SLM-printed Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni alloys corresponding to P-70, P-90, P-110, P-130 and P-150, and that (f) is the longitudinal section of P-110.
The citing text attributes the fine equiaxed grains with random orientations to the use of a rotation angle of 67° for each printing layer during the SLM process.
The citing text states that columnar grains dominate the vertical section of the P-110 sample, with a small amount of equiaxed grains mainly distributed at the bottom of the melt pool.

The citing text explains the columnar growth by vertical heat flow along the deposition direction and partial remelting of the solidified layer producing well-aligned periodic melt pools through which columnar grains extend to adjacent layers.
The sample-to-panel assignment (P-70 to P-150) is not printed inside the maps themselves and can only be obtained from the caption.

measured_quantities: crystallographic orientation / texture via IPF colouring (dimensionless)
unreadable_items: No illegible elements at the supplied resolution; note that the sample identity of each map (P-70 ... P-150) is not printed on the panels and comes from the caption, and grain sizes are not quantified numerically on any panel.
